published_prior_art.cite: Goff2026OutcomeNonrestrictive: gives a brute-force two-factor WARP application, not a symbolic three-factor classification.
Goff2026OutcomeNonrestrictive: Section 6 enumerates nine two-factor WARP types; no three-factor zero-Mobius 29-map classification.
Goff2026OutcomeNonrestrictive proves the two-factor maximal four-type support, while BlackwellPashley2023FactorialIV retains factor-specific receipt; neither gives the three-factor 29-map envelope.
BlackwellPashley2023FactorialIV identifies perfect-complier factorial effects under treatment exclusion; the displayed signed formulas are new only through validity on Theorem 2's wider support.
Goff2026OutcomeNonrestrictive supplies an abstract row-space necessity result, not the proposed nondegenerate Bernoulli observational-equivalence witness for every excluded three-factor WARP type.
BlackwellPashley2023FactorialIV develops factorial-IV superpopulation inference; this is a routine joint delta-method adaptation.
BlackwellPashley2023FactorialIV and KangPeckKeele2018RandomizationIV provide nearby ratio-inversion logic; the Bonferroni Walsh image is a routine inference rung.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorems 1-2 give finite-support sufficiency and necessity for outcome-nonrestrictive identification; Section 6 enumerates nine two-factor WARP types and Proposition 6 identifies the four-type coordinate-separable support as maximal for the two-factor local interaction.

source_verification_receipts.version: accepted author manuscript corresponding to JASA 118(542), 1102-1114; publisher version was not text-accessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Treatment exclusion makes each factor's uptake depend only on its own assignment and rules out interactive receipt; §2.4 defines perfect-complier factorial effects and their ratio representation.
The paper studies unordered monotonicity in discrete choice and states its equivalence with additive separability of treatment-choice equations in observed and unobserved variables.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a compact worked table giving the six fully interactive null maps, their strict rankings, and every Mobius signature; this makes the claimed strict extension independently auditable.
Obtain and audit Blackwell--Pashley supplement C, then state explicitly whether its weaker treatment-exclusion discussion excludes each of the six fully interactive maps.
Develop the deferred arbitrary-K recursion or contrast-specific envelope classification; either would turn the fixed-K field contribution into a broader mathematical program.

recommended_next_step: Advance the three-factor maximal-envelope angle to Stage 0, retaining the inference statements as supporting rungs rather than novelty claims.
